summary: The article accurately reports on the Indian government's recent tax exemption for FIIs and BIS on interest income and capital gains from G-Secs, effective retrospectively from April 1, 2026, and correctly outlines the mechanisms for foreign investment.

claims.claim: The Indian government has exempted Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) from taxes on interest income and capital gains derived from Indian Government Securities (G-Secs).
claims.note: The Indian government has introduced a retrospective tax exemption for FIIs on government securities income, waiving taxes on interest income and capital gains.

claims.claim: This policy change, effective retrospectively from April 1, 2026, could have a positive ripple effect on bond yields and overall market sentiment in India.
claims.note: The Income-tax (Amendment) Ordinance, 2026, promulgated on June 5, 2026, made this tax relief effective retrospectively from April 1, 2026.

claims.claim: Introduced in 2020, the FAR allows non-resident investors to invest in specified G-Secs without any restrictions on the quantum of investment.
claims.note: The Fully Accessible Route (FAR) was introduced by the RBI in 2020 and allows unrestricted foreign investment in select Government of India securities without quantitative caps.

claims.claim: The VRR was introduced in 2019 to encourage long-term foreign investment in Indian debt markets.
claims.note: The Voluntary Retention Route (VRR) was introduced by the RBI on March 1, 2019, to encourage long-term foreign investment in Indian debt markets.

claims.claim: Under VRR, FPIs commit to investing a certain amount in Indian debt for a minimum retention period, typically three years.
claims.note: The minimum retention period for investment under VRR is three years.

claims.claim: Both routes require FIIs (now generally referred to as Foreign Portfolio Investors or FPIs) to register with SEBI.
claims.note: FIIs, now referred to as FPIs, need to register with SEBI through a Designated Depository Participant (DDP).

claims.claim: The eligibility for this exemption is generally tied to FIIs registered as Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) with SEBI, and also extends to the Bank for International Settlements (BIS).
claims.note: The exemption applies to FIIs (FPIs) and the Bank for International Settlements (BIS).

article_title: FII Tax Exemption on G-Secs: What Changed and Why it Matters
